purpose: Answer key for the first production research cycle (approvals A26 and A34). It is frozen before any analysis of this target, by the deployed system or any other AgentSmith code.
status: FROZEN before analysis. It must not be edited after the run; any correction is a separate, dated adjudication record that quotes the entry, and the original reading is always reported (as in T-205).
authoredBy: the orchestrating Claude Code session, from reading the level sources at the pinned commit. Not from Ethernaut's tests, attack contracts or descriptions, and not from any AgentSmith output.

target.note: the pinned commit is the default branch head on 2026-11-27. Branch 'main' points to a different commit (c6174bb) and is not used.

snapshotBoundary.method: buildPlan() from the deployed commit 837aeb9, run on the commit's git tree with default limits

excludedReason.contracts/test: Foundry tests, which contain the reference solutions

snapshotBoundary.note: excluded files still appear as manifest rows marked excluded_by_policy, with their git object id, but their content is not stored and the analyser never reads them. The analyser reads every stored .sol file.

scoring.unit: (contract.function | class), as the analyser emits hypotheses
scoring.detected: an expected entry is detected when any of its acceptedKeys appears as a hypothesis in the run; whether the evidence span overlaps the expected lines is reported separately
scoring.recall: detected / 14 expected entries (in the analyser's classes); out-of-scope levels are reported, never scored as misses
scoring.unkeyedHypotheses: every hypothesis matching neither an expected key nor a pre-listed adjudication key is listed and judged by hand as a false positive or a genuine unlisted issue, with a reason; none is dropped
scoring.infrastructure: hypotheses in factories, helpers, metrics, proxy or Ethernaut.sol are reported in their own section
scoring.challengeOutcomes: the deterministic challenge outcomes (supports, refutes, inconclusive) are reported per hypothesis, not scored
scoring.confirmed: stays 0 in this cycle: confirmation needs a human adjudication, which the deployed system cannot record

exposure.codeLevel: none found. No Ethernaut-specific code, names or identifiers appear in AgentSmith's evaluation corpora, fixtures, tests or analyser source, at the branch head, at the deployed commit or anywhere in history. The only shared lines are standard OpenZeppelin proxy and Ownable boilerplate (eval/heldout3 and heldout4).
exposure.patternLevel: present. The analyser was developed on eval/dev and corrected on crytic/not-so-smart-contracts (eval/real-runs), which contain textbook versions of the same patterns (reentrancy, tx.origin, unprotected owner setters, misnamed constructors).
exposure.authorship: present. The analyser's rules and this answer key were written by Claude-family sessions, and Ethernaut (public since 2018) is very likely in that model family's training data. The key is therefore not independent of the analyser's author.
exposure.qualification: exposure-qualified: code-blind but pattern-familiar, with a same-family-authored answer key. The cycle proves operation, not detection ability. Its scores are not a clean measurement. The key can be checked independently against Ethernaut's own tests and attack contracts, which were excluded from the snapshot and not used to write it.

expected.intendedFlaw: receive() makes any sender with a non-zero contribution the owner; withdraw() is then open to them
the intended constructor is misspelled, so Fal1out() is a public function that sets owner
authorisation by tx.origin != msg.sender: any contract relaying a call becomes able to set owner
fallback() delegatecalls arbitrary msg.data into Delegate, whose pwn() overwrites Delegation's owner slot
external call to msg.sender (line 21) before the balance is reduced (line 25)
delegatecall into a library whose storage layout differs, overwriting timeZone1Library and then owner
anyone can selfdestruct the token and send its ether to any address
the partner call (line 19) forwards all gas and its result is ignored; a partner that consumes all gas denies the owner's withdrawal
expected.note: the intended flaw is gas-griefing denial of service; unchecked-call is the closest analyser class

expected.intendedFlaw: the Engine implementation is never initialised in its own storage; anyone can call initialize() on it, become upgrader and upgradeToAndCall into a destructive implementation
misnamed public 'constructor' lets anyone set owner
the WETH transferFrom low-level call result (line 27) is returned but never required; stake is credited even when no tokens move
mintNFTEOA has no reentrancy guard; _mintNFT calls the receiver hook (line 32) before _mint, so the one-per-address balance check can be re-entered
expected.note: tx.origin == msg.sender no longer proves an EOA (EIP-7702); either reading counts

expected.intendedFlaw: ether is sent to msg.sender (line 92) before the wrapped tokens are burned; nonReentrant guards withdrawAll only, not the rest of the protocol
expected.note: cross-function reentrancy; my confidence in the exact intended path is medium

expected.intendedFlaw: a standalone copy of SimpleToken: anyone can selfdestruct it
expected.note: same flaw as EXP-07, in a separate file; scored separately
